profiled_workloads.selection_reason: Largest low-speedup fp16 case (4096x4096, 16.78M elements); primary target for the device-time and pipeline-overlap question.
Same element count and byte volume as timing-3 but bf16; needed to separate byte-driven cost from log-instruction cost.
Worst speedup and highest latency of the whole round; fp32 8192-element tile regime, the case that discriminates byte-scaling from instruction-count scaling.
Small-shape control: 8 KiB of traffic cannot occupy 12.4 us of device time, so this bounds how much of the small-case latency is host launch overhead.

performance_interpretation: NO PROFILER COUNTERS WERE OBTAINED THIS ROUND, so questions 1-3 (device vs full-call split, MTE2/MTE3/Vector active ratios, bank-conflict or spill evidence) CANNOT be answered from measurement; any figure for them would be invented. What CAN be established uses only authoritative eval latencies from get_profile_context plus workload specs from hgkda_workloads, with the arithmetic below labeled as inference. (i) Small cases carry almost no device cost: timing-0 is float16 [1024] = 4 KiB read + 4 KiB written = 8 KiB total traffic; at the measured 12.3927 us that is 0.33 GB/s effective, and the 10.2833 us reference on the same 8 KiB shows the harness floor is ~10 us. So essentially all of the 12.4 us and the whole 0.83 speedup is host launch/dispatch cost, and roughly 2.1 us of extra host work versus the reference is the entire small-case deficit. (ii) Large-case cost is byte-driven, not log-instruction-driven: all three large cases execute exactly 16,777,216 tl.log evaluations with an identical op mix modulo dtype conversion, yet candidate per-element time is 2.5519 ns (fp16), 2.6482 ns (bf16, +3.8% at identical bytes) and 4.6094 ns (fp32), i.e. the fp32/fp16 time ratio is 1.806 for a 2.0x per-element byte ratio. Time tracks bytes while the log count is constant, which contradicts competing hypothesis (b) that the tl.log lowering is the dominant limiter. (iii) Logical effective throughput computed as 2 x bytes-per-element x elements / latency: candidate 1.57 TB/s (fp16), 1.51 TB/s (bf16), 1.74 TB/s (fp32); reference 4.24 TB/s, 2.65 TB/s, 5.20 TB/s on the identical shapes, dtypes, in-place storage and measurement harness. Because the reference reaches 2.7-3.0x the candidate's logical rate on the same data, competing hypothesis (d) 'simple GM bandwidth saturation' is contradicted as an explanation of the gap: the memory system demonstrably sustains at least the reference's rate, and the candidate sits near one third of it. (iv) UB pressure, hypothesis (c), has no positive evidence: the fp32 tile is 8192 elements = 32 KiB source and the 2-byte tile 16384 elements = 32 KiB source (64 KiB once staged to fp32), both far below the 192 KiB UB, the kernel compiles and passes all 36 workloads, and fp32 - which uses the SMALLER tile - shows the HIGHEST effective throughput, the opposite of what a large-tile UB-pressure story predicts. (v) That leaves hypothesis (a) as the leading candidate at medium confidence, without counters: with 2048 programs (fp32) and 1024 programs (2-byte) on 20 AI cores the grid is ~51-102 waves, so parallelism is not scarce, but each program performs exactly one monolithic tl.load of the whole tile, one vector chain and one monolithic tl.store, leaving no loop body for Triton's software pipeliner to multi-buffer, so per core the sequence is MTE2-wait -> V -> MTE3-drain with no cross-iteration overlap; the measured 1.5-1.7 TB/s is consistent with approximately serialized transfer phases, whereas full overlap would approach the 2.6-5.2 TB/s the reference demonstrates. The round's frozen hypothesis (strided-path correctness plus a reusable compiled launcher for small shapes) is already settled by the eval rather than by profiling: 36/36 PASSED including correctness-7/15/23, with small-case latency down to the ~12.4 us floor. Profiler evidence therefore neither supports nor contradicts the frozen hypothesis; it is simply unavailable.

next_experiment.action_description: In _log10_flat and _log10_flat_masked, replace the single monolithic tl.load(x_ptr + offs) / tl.store(x_ptr + offs, ...) over the whole BLOCK with an inner loop over sub-tiles inside the same program: keep the outer tile and grid (block = 8192 elements for 4-byte dtypes, 16384 for 2-byte dtypes, grid = cdiv(n, block) as today), and iterate CHUNK = 2048 elements (4-byte) / 4096 elements (2-byte) via 'for k in tl.range(0, BLOCK, CHUNK, num_stages=2)', loading, staging to fp32, computing tl.log(x) * 0.4342944819032518 and storing each CHUNK inside the loop body. Keep the in-place pointer (same address for load and store; each chunk reads and writes only its own disjoint addresses, so there is no loop-carried dependency), keep the fp32 staging that the correctness contract depends on, and keep the mask only on the final partial program (or reuse _log10_flat_masked for that tail) so the fast path stays unmasked. Leave _log10_scaled and _log10_nd untouched. Do not change _pick_block, the entry cache, the stream resolution or the direct-launcher call signature.
next_experiment.expected_impact: Expected effect is derived from eval-latency arithmetic in performance_interpretation, NOT from profiler counters (none were collected this round). If each program's load, compute and store phases begin to overlap across loop iterations, effective logical throughput should move from the measured 1.51-1.74 TB/s toward the 2.65-5.20 TB/s the reference achieves on the identical workloads: timing-11 from 77.3 us toward 45-55 us, timing-3 from 42.8 us toward 28-34 us, timing-7 from 44.4 us toward 30-36 us, for a projected geo_mean of roughly 0.78-0.85 versus the current 0.6799, with timing-0 unchanged because it is entirely host-bound.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: Risks: (1) the Ascend backend may ignore num_stages or fail to multi-buffer this loop body, in which case the change is performance-neutral and the chunk loop only adds scalar index arithmetic; (2) multi-buffering multiplies UB demand by the stage count - 2 stages x 2048 fp32 would be 16 KiB in plus 8-16 KiB out per buffer, still far below 192 KiB, but confirm no UB overflow before trusting the result; (3) a smaller CHUNK reduces the vector-op width per iteration, which could cost throughput if the vector unit is better fed by one wide op - mitigate by starting at CHUNK=2048/4096 and only then trying 1024 if UB or code size complains. Rollback: this change is confined to the two contiguous-path @triton.jit bodies; keep the current tmp/main.py as the revert point and restore the monolithic single-load body if any large case regresses.
success_criteria: All 36 workloads PASSED, including the strided cases correctness-7/15/23 and the empty/1-element cases, with the in-place contract intact (same tensor object returned, parent-storage padding untouched).
Headline geo_mean strictly greater than the current 0.6799, target >= 0.78.
log10_-timing-11 latency below 60 us (from 77.33 us) and log10_-timing-3 below 34 us (from 42.81 us); log10_-timing-7 below 36 us (from 44.43 us).
No small-shape regression: log10_-timing-0/4/8 stay within ~0.5 us of their current 12.3-13.2 us, since they are host-bound and must not pay for the device-side change.
Non-finite and NaN/Inf semantics unchanged versus the round-1 passing result (no new mismatch at any correctness uuid).
